purpose: Register external failure-analysis, anomaly-classification and incident/adverse-event reporting authorities identified during comparison of VIGIL failure-mode records and the Caelestis runtime failure taxonomy. Registration is for terminology, reporting architecture and comparative failure-analysis support. It does not infer unseen normative requirements, CAM applicability, or conformance.

sources.title: Failure modes and effects analysis (FMEA and FMECA)
sources.notes: Current IEC publisher metadata describes a generic FMEA/FMECA method applicable to hardware, software, processes, human action and interfaces, including failure modes, local/global effects, causes, criticality and reporting formats. Registered as supporting failure-analysis authority; normative clauses were not reviewed.

sources.title: IEEE Standard Classification for Software Anomalies
sources.notes: Historical software-anomaly classification authority retained for terminology and causal-analysis comparison. IEEE marks the standard inactive-reserved as of 2020-03-05; it is not treated as a current conformance baseline.

sources.title: Systems and software engineering — Vocabulary
sources.notes: Common systems/software engineering vocabulary. The 2017 edition remains the published standard but ISO records it as to be revised; Edition 3 is under development. Registered for terminology harmonisation, not for unseen normative reconstruction.

sources.title: Towards a common reporting framework for AI incidents
sources.notes: AI-specific common reporting framework with 29 reporting criteria, retained as a direct public supporting authority for incident-reporting interoperability and terminology. It is not a binding standard.

sources.title: Accident/Incident Data Reporting (ADREP) Taxonomy
sources.notes: Cross-sector reporting exemplar using multiple attributes and common definitions for accident/incident reporting. ICAO states that the taxonomy is being updated. Retained for comparative reporting architecture, not AI conformance.

sources.title: Terminologies for Categorized Adverse Event Reporting (AER): terms, terminology and codes
sources.notes: Current international medical-device adverse-event terminology separates device problem, investigation type, investigation findings, investigation conclusion, health effects and component. Retained as a mature faceted reporting exemplar, not as an AI standard.

sources.title: Medical Device Reporting (MDR) Adverse Event Codes
sources.notes: Regulatory adverse-event coding exemplar with separate hierarchical categories for device problem, component, investigation type, investigation findings, investigation conclusion, clinical signs/conditions and health impact. FDA states the codes are harmonized with IMDRF terminology. Retained as comparative reporting architecture.

source_scope_updates.extraction_scope_notes: Registered for FMEA/FMECA failure-mode, effects, cause, criticality and reporting-structure comparison. No clause-level normative extraction is claimed.
source_scope_updates.next_action: Use as a terminology and method cross-reference; obtain lawful primary text only if clause-level conformance analysis becomes necessary.

source_scope_updates.extraction_scope_notes: Historical software-anomaly classification reference; IEEE marks the standard inactive-reserved. No current conformance claim or clause extraction is intended.
source_scope_updates.next_action: Retain for terminology/history and causal-analysis comparison.

source_scope_updates.extraction_scope_notes: Registered as systems/software vocabulary authority. No definitions beyond lawfully available publisher material are reconstructed.
source_scope_updates.next_action: Monitor Edition 3 development and use the published 2017 identity for terminology cross-reference until superseded.

source_scope_updates.extraction_scope_notes: AI-specific incident-reporting framework retained for reporting-dimension and interoperability comparison, not as a binding requirement baseline.
source_scope_updates.next_action: Crosswalk VIGIL failure-report fields against OECD reporting criteria without converting policy guidance into mandatory duties.

source_scope_updates.extraction_scope_notes: Cross-sector accident/incident taxonomy exemplar retained for multi-axis reporting architecture and common-language comparison.
source_scope_updates.next_action: Use only as comparative reporting architecture; monitor ICAO taxonomy revision.

source_scope_updates.extraction_scope_notes: Cross-sector adverse-event terminology exemplar retained for separation of problem, investigation, finding, conclusion, effect and component dimensions.
source_scope_updates.next_action: Use for comparative failure-report ontology design; do not infer AI-specific requirements.

source_scope_updates.extraction_scope_notes: Regulatory adverse-event coding exemplar retained for reporting-axis comparison and explicit preservation of unresolved investigation states.
source_scope_updates.next_action: Use as comparative reporting architecture; rely on IMDRF for the international terminology lineage.
